sources: TUESDAY Sep 22 2026 RUN. HEADLINE: the yield curve is the story. 2s10s at 0.20 is the flattest of 2026 and only 20bp from inversion, 5bp flatter on the day and down from 0.25 in the prior file, driven by the 2y repricing to 4.76 pct (a cycle high) as the Fed hikes into sticky inflation while the 10y eases 4bp to 4.951 pct. Everything else in the risk complex stays benign or improved. FRESH THIS RUN: 2s10s 0.20 (24/7 Wall St macro release; 2y 4.76 pct, 10y just above 5 pct before easing on Sep 22). HY OAS 276bp (FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 daily, Sep 15; FRED monthly Sep prints 270, so a modest widening). VIX 16.20 (Sep 21 close, up from 14.87) - CAVEAT: Sep 22 was a strong risk-on session (S&P +1.49 pct to 7,764.70, Nasdaq +2.26 pct to a record 27,122.09, Dow +0.71 pct, AI complex leading with Intel +12 pct and AMD +10 pct through a 1trn market cap), so the Sep 22 VIX close was very likely lower than 16.20; no dated Sep 22 print was located. DXY 100.37 (FXStreet Sep 21, +0.15 pct d/d, up more than 1 pct over the prior week as markets digest the Fed's return to hiking - target range raised 25bp to 3.75-4.00 pct with further tightening signalled). Copper 6.65 USD/lb and gold spot 4,309 USD/oz give copper/gold 1.54 (TradingEconomics, CNBC/Fortune). 5y5y breakevens 2.33 (FRED T5YIFR, Sep 2026). BRENT DATA FLAG: quoted at 101.24 but vendors disagree materially - Arbiterz/TradingEconomics put Brent at 101.40 on Mon Sep 21 and near 101.24 on Sep 22, TradingEconomics separately quoted a Sep 21 low of 100.06, and the prior automated run wrote 95.96 at 21:52 UTC Sep 21. The 96-101 band is timing/vendor noise; the DIRECTION is unambiguous - this is the fourth consecutive down session, after Trump held off on striking Yemen and signalled openness to Iran diplomacy, plus signs of recovering Saudi exports. Brent has now unwound essentially the entire Sep 15 geopolitical spike from 130.80. CARRIED: MOVE 81.2 (MacroMicro, no fresh dated print). NFCI -0.56 for the week ending Sep 11, unchanged (Chicago Fed; next release Wed Sep 23). Initial claims 196k for the week ending Sep 12, 4-week average 203.25k (DOL; next release Thu Sep 24). ISM manufacturing 54.6 (August, released Sep 2). UMich consumer sentiment 47.8 (September preliminary; final Sep 25). Building permits 1,394k (August, Census/HUD). LEI y/y approx -0.7 pct (Conference Board, August). Sahm rule -0.07 (FRED SAHMREALTIME). SOFR-OIS 0bp and EUR/USD 3M xccy basis -10bp remain carried assumptions with no free live source. Global liquidity held at 1 (stable). BDTI DATA FLAG: carried at 4,899 and NOT confirmed for a second consecutive run. Investing.com quotes 1,107 while MacroMicro history shows the index above 1,900 at an all-time high in May 2026. The 4,899 level cannot be reconciled with either vendor and should be treated as STALE / LOW CONFIDENCE until a dated Baltic Exchange print resolves the series. PICTURE: risk gauges remain benign - VIX in the mid-teens, MOVE ~81, credit tight at 276bp, NFCI at the loosest of the cycle, claims at 196k and equities at record highs - while the curve flattens toward zero. The soft spots are unchanged and domestic: UMich 47.8 near record lows, LEI negative y/y, permits falling. WATCH: NFCI (Sep 23), claims (Sep 24), UMich final September (Sep 25), ISM (Oct 1), and above all whether 2s10s inverts. SOURCES: FRED/St. Louis Fed (T10Y2Y, T5YIFR, VIXCLS, BAMLH0A0HYM2, NFCI, ICSA, SAHMREALTIME, PERMIT, UMCSENT), Chicago Fed, TradingEconomics, Investing.com, Arbiterz, MacroRadar, 24/7 Wall St, FXStreet, CNBC, Fortune, Cboe, MacroMicro (MOVE, BDTI), US Department of Labor, Conference Board, ISM, University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers, Census Bureau/HUD, Schwab.
